analysis:
Examined all supplied metadata, patches, source, declarations, tests and documentation. The workflow activates a fixed HTTPS desktop update feed while retaining existing signing, team, notarization and bundle-identity checks (.github/workflows/release-desktop.yml:129,173-192). electron-builder.ts:23-31 now refuses releases without a feed; preview isolation remains intact. update-feed.mjs:12-51 restamps post-signing DMG hashes and checks locally parsed entries against SHA-512 and size. Tests cover normal feed shape, stale hashes, version mismatch and release configuration. No supported authorization, encryption, prompt/cache exposure, billing or privileged-helper regression is established by this scope; T-041 controls are untouched.
Integration must examine the newly activated remote executable-update contract against TB-003, T-013/T-043 and the distinction between artifact identity and serving qualification in TB-011/T-054. Runtime feed parsing, downloaded-app signature/identity enforcement, downgrade policy and quit/install interactions are not supplied; their absence is not proof of missing controls.
Two concrete publication questions remain: tests/updateFeedFile.test.ts:7-14 describes a versioned DMG URL and top-level path, but workflow:244-246 uploads only a versionless DMG alongside the versioned ZIP. Confirm whether runtime consumers exclusively select the ZIP before treating the missing advertised DMG as a security-relevant availability defect. Also workflow:25 serializes per ref, whereas :246 overwrites one shared manifest without version ordering; assess out-of-order release publication and security-update reachability. The regex checker validates recognized entries, not full YAML semantics or the uploaded asset set, so it does not resolve these questions. No finding is asserted without the relevant runtime contract.
